binders: Two constant states q_l and q_r in the state space of the selected hyperbolic equation.
An initial state function x |-> q(x,0).
definitions_and_conventions: q_l is the constant left state and q_r is the constant right state.
The subscripts l and r denote the sides of the jump, not derivatives.
The interface is placed at x = 0 by convention ('say x = 0'); a translated interface is not part of the displayed equation (1.11).
When used between neighboring finite-volume cells, the source sets q_l = Q_{i-1} and q_r = Q_i.
hypotheses: The Riemann problem consists of a hyperbolic equation supplied with piecewise-constant initial data having its interface at x = 0.
implicit_context: The data is one-dimensional and is initial data at time t = 0.
The states may be scalar or vector-valued according to the underlying hyperbolic equation.
The value at the single interface point is immaterial to the piecewise-constant left/right specification used for conservation-law solutions, but the source simply leaves it unstated.

details: Each open half-line carries one constant state.
The sole interface is at the origin, separating x < 0 from x > 0.
Adjacent cell averages supply the two states for an interface Riemann problem.

undebatable_constraints: The left branch is q_l on the strict inequality x < 0.
The right branch is q_r on the strict inequality x > 0.
No x = 0 branch may be attributed to equation (1.11).
The data is initial data q(x,0), not a time-independent formula asserted for all t.
The states are constant on their respective half-lines.
The special data belongs together with a hyperbolic equation to form the Riemann problem.
